subject: Vectorly Labs — Redwood SDK adapter & joint PoC plan
messages:
From: Maya Santos <maya@vectorly.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: partnerships@vectorly.com
Date: 2026-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Vectorly x Redwood — SDK adapter proposal + draft SOW

Hi Ava,

Great to meet you at DevCon last week. Vectorly Labs is excited about building a formal integration with Redwood so our orchestration flows can call Redwood-hosted models with first-class tracing and prompt telemetry. We put together a short draft SOW and an API surface doc to kick off planning — attaching both.

High-level ask: can Redwood evaluate a small PoC (2–3 weeks) to ship a LangChain adapter and an index connector for LlamaIndex that also emits standardized trace events we can consume in our observability dashboard? Key success criteria would be:
- Bi-directional streaming with correct function-calling when using Redwood streaming endpoints
- Trace events for request start/stop, model variant, token counts, and per-chunk latency
- A minimal sample showing LlamaIndex using Redwood embeddings reliably at scale (100k tokens/day)

We’d love to run a discovery call next week and align on scope, timelines, and who owns the SOW redlines. Do you have availability Wed/Thu morning PST?

Attachments: Vectorly_Redwood_SDK_SOW_v1.pdf, vectorly-api-surface.md

Cheers,
Maya Santos
Head of Partnerships, Vectorly Labs
M: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Santos <maya@vectorly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-19T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vectorly x Redwood — SDK adapter proposal + draft SOW

Maya — thanks for the note and the SOW. PDF looks tidy; API surface doc is helpful. Ben and Marissa are looped in from partnerships and platform-integration. Quick responses to the asks below and a proposal for next steps.

Short answers to your success criteria:
- Streaming/function-calling: Redwood streaming endpoints support function calling and an adapter is straightforward, but we need to agree on the function schema and how Vectorly wants to present tools to end users.
- Trace events: we can emit standardized trace hooks (start/stop/event metadata) and include token accounting. We’ll need your preferred event schema; we typically send JSON over an HTTP collector or via Kafka for partners.
- LlamaIndex connector: we can build a connector that swaps remote embedding calls to Redwood — should be low friction.

Proposed next steps:
1) Discovery call (30–45m) to align on adapter surface + security requirements — Wed 2026-01-21 09:00 or Thu 2026-01-22 10:00 PST.
2) Technical spec: Ben will draft a concise adapter spec outlining the adapter API and trace hooks within 3 business days of the call.
3) PoC SOW: Marissa will take the SOW and propose engineering estimates and acceptance criteria.

Pre-call ask for Vectorly: sample request/response with your desired trace event fields, and any sandbox credentials for Redwood to use during the PoC.

A couple of immediate constraints to flag:
- For the PoC we can use Redwood-hosted dev instances but production traffic that includes PII will require a Dedicated or Private deployment and additional controls (KMS integration, VPC).
- If Vectorly needs persistent audit logs kept beyond our default retention, we’ll need a support add-on in the SOW.

Ben/Marissa — any additions?

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Partner Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Santos <maya@vectorly.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-20T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vectorly x Redwood — SDK adapter proposal + draft SOW

On Tue, Jan 19, 2026 at 2:05 PM Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Maya — thanks for the note and the SOW. PDF looks tidy; API surface doc is helpful. Ben and Marissa are looped in from partnerships and platform-integration. Quick responses to the asks below and a proposal for next steps.

Thanks Ava — Wed 01/21 9:00 PST works for our engineering lead (Lucas) and myself. We attached a short example payload that shows the trace fields we prefer (trace_id, span_id, model_variant, tokens_request, tokens_response, latency_ms, tool_invocations). We’re fine with either HTTP collector or a Kafka topic — for the PoC HTTP is easiest.

Security notes: we do not want any customer PII in trace payloads by default; we will send identifiers that are hashed (sha256) on our side. If Redwood requires more info for debugging we’ll set up a temporary secure share via DocuSign/audit-approved channel. Vectorly is happy to sign a narrow NDA addendum for the PoC if that expedites access to a staging dataset.

I also added a short repo stub (in the attachments) showing a LangChain adapter skeleton and a LlamaIndex connector pattern. We’d like to jointly publish a reference repo after the PoC.

Attachments: example-repo-link.txt (link + README excerpt)

See you on Wed.

—Maya
Maya Santos
Head of Partnerships, Vectorly Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Santos <maya@vectorly.com>
Date: 2026-01-21T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vectorly x Redwood — SDK adapter proposal + draft SOW

Forwarded message: see below for prep notes for tomorrow’s discovery.

Key engineering assumptions / risks:
- Tracing: we should align on a minimal stable schema for the PoC. Vectorly’s suggested fields look fine. We’ll implement an optional enrichment point for model metadata (quantization tag, kernel selection) that we can include if partners opt in.
- Performance: LangChain adapter must support continuous batching to avoid per-token cost blowup. The PoC should include a small workload test (1k concurrent requests over 30 minutes) to surface batching behavior.
- Authentication: we’ll provide scoped API keys for PoC. Production will require token rotation and integration with your SSO if you want deeper ops access.

Estimated effort (rough): 3 wks eng (1 engineer full-time) + 1 wk QA + docs + reference sample. If Vectorly wants an accelerated timeline we can add another engineer but that increases cost.

Action items before the call:
- Vectorly: send example trace payloads (Maya did this) and link to your reference repo (received).
- Redwood: draft adapter spec (I’ll do a 1–2 page spec) and a minimal test plan.

I’ll attach an internal checklist in the shared folder after the call.

Ben Carter
Partner Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Santos <maya@vectorly.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-22T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vectorly x Redwood — SDK adapter proposal + draft SOW

Thanks everyone — good alignment on scope. Confirming the discovery call for Wed 2026-01-21 09:00 PST (calendar invite sent). Recap / owners and pre-kickoff deliverables:

Owners:
- Redwood: Ben Carter (adapter spec & PoC infra), Marissa Cole (SOW + commercial terms)
- Vectorly: Maya Santos (partnership owner), Lucas R. (eng lead for repo work)

Pre-kickoff deliverables (please deliver by Tue 2026-01-20 EOD):
- Vectorly: final example trace payloads (JSON), sandbox API key for Redwood PoC, and the repo stub link (we have the README excerpt already).
- Redwood: initial 1–2 page adapter spec (Ben), draft PoC acceptance criteria (Marissa).

Meeting goals (30–45m): align on acceptance criteria, decide PoC environment (hosted dev vs. dedicated), agree on milestone dates, and clarify any compliance constraints (data retention, audit logs).

Note on compliance: as discussed, if Vectorly wants traces with hashed identifiers that should satisfy our usual dev environment rules. Production traces that include customer identifiers will require Private deployment or a dedicated contract addendum.

I’ll upload the draft SOW to the shared drive after Marissa’s initial redline.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
